purpose: Human-reviewable plan consumed by Scripts/release_aron_poles.py: strip the north-south carrying poles from the CC BY-SA davidgra11 Aron body (GeometryScript, duplicate asset), build one gold east-west pole (capsule) and place two of them beside the Aron so they reach the paroches (Yoma 54a / Menachot 98a-b, Rashi Shemot 25:12), swapping RELEASE_Aron_Body to the pole-less duplicate. Every number below comes from an offline parse of the frozen OBJ, the import/rotate/doors receipts or the sources quoted in 'sources'; nothing here claims visual acceptance.
lastKnownMapSha256Note: Walkthrough.umap on disk at 2026-09-07 16:40 local while the ShulchanV2 import (SourceAssets/vessels-review/ShulchanV2/native-import-20260907T203842904337Z.json) was still running; other native jobs keep changing the map, so this is recorded as matched/not matched only, never a guard. The body actor's mesh/pose/bounds and the paroches bounds are verified at run time instead. Run this script only when no other native job is active.
collisionNote: Both poles NoCollision like the vessels: the Kodesh is not on the visitor route and the poles cross the Kodesh doorway and the paroches (a NoCollision curtain) on purpose.

source.connectedComponentsNote: Offline union-find over the welded OBJ: ONE component. The poles are fused to the ring bores (216 shared vertices at |y| 34..36 mm), so GeometryScript connected-component splitting cannot isolate them; the rule below is geometric (distance from the pole axis plus outward-normal test).

bodyMesh.importedTrianglesNote: native-import-vessels-20260907T190204035803Z.json: 110 sliver triangles lost to remove_degenerates; the importer mirrored local Y (asset units = file mm read as cm).
bodyMesh.windingConvention: UE face normal cross(C-A, B-A) points outward on the imported asset (winding receipt: signed volume +42024.4, 0 disagreements over all 715138 triangles). The raw OBJ is right-handed: cross(B-A, C-A) outward.

poleRule.note: Model poles: two cylinders along local Y at x = +-24.1 mm, z = 36.86 mm, radius 1.85-1.91 mm, spanning y +-61.375 mm; the body ends at |y| = 42.52 mm (lower moulding), walls at |y| <= 39.4. A triangle is a pole triangle when its centroid lies within poleInnerRadius of its side's pole axis, OR within poleOuterRadius with a face normal pointing AWAY from the axis (radial dot > outwardDotMin); ring-bore triangles in the same band point TOWARD the axis and stay. Axes are re-derived in the engine from the pole-tip corners (|y| > tipMinAbsY) and must match 'axes' within axisToleranceFileUnits.
poleRule.axesNote: [x, z, maxRadius] of the pole cross-section per side from the tip vertices (|y| > 45).
poleRule.keptBoundsNote: X extent stays +-27.06 because the four rings (on the local +-X faces, axis along Y) remain; Y shrinks from +-61.375 (pole tips) to the body's lower moulding +-42.5; Z unchanged.
poleRule.tubeSelfCheckNote: Among sure pole-tube triangles (centroid distance < 1.8, |y| < 60) at least this fraction must have an outward radial normal under the engine convention; otherwise the handedness assumption is wrong and the run refuses.

ringRule.note: Optional: also delete the four empty rings (centroid |x| > minAbsX in the ring z band, |y| < maxAbsY, not pole). Not default: the rings are unioned into the wall so deleting them leaves ring-footprint holes in the wall; kept rings are recorded as a limitation (empty rings on the east/west faces, axis north-south, not threaded by the new east-west poles).
ringRule.expectedRingTrianglesNote: Informational (offline 2026-09-07): 3839 ring-body triangles plus 426 ring-bore band triangles inside the ring region; 171 band triangles outside it stay.
ringRule.expectedKeptBoundsIfDeletedNote: Offline 2026-09-07: the ring-bore band is deleted with the rings; the remaining X extent is the carved panel frames (asymmetric by 0.06 mm in the source).

poles.meshNote: One capsule pole along local X, origin at its centre, used by both actors. Project geometry (not third-party): lives beside the earlier procedural Aron parts.
poles.axes: X east, Y south, Z up (project convention): the north pole has negative Y.
poles.yRule: poleCentreY = +-(bodyHalfLengthWorld + radius + gapCm), bodyHalfLengthWorld = max |y| of the pole-less body (42.5187 mm) x 1.471 = 62.55 cm. The poles lie along the OUTSIDE of the two short (north/south) faces: Rashi Shemot 25:12 - rings at the upper corners, two on each side across the WIDTH of the Aron, the LENGTH of the Aron (2.5 amot) separating pole from pole; Menachot 98b - the poles lay across the width so two carriers walked between them. With the length north-south the poles therefore run east-west beside the north and south faces.
poles.zRule: poleCentreZ = body origin Z + model pole axis z (36.859 mm) x 1.471 = 925 + 54.22 = 979.22 cm; the model's own ring height (upper part of the 72.3 cm body, Rashi: 'at the upper corners near the kaporet'). The task's 'lower third, +25 cm' guess is NOT used; recorded.
poles.xRule: West end = body west extent (rings included, -6239.8) - westStubCm; east end = eastEndX, which must lie inside the paroches cloth's X range (the poles press into the curtain 'like two breasts', Yoma 54a). Length = eastEndX - westEnd (~680 cm, 13.6 amot at 50 cm). The brief's 300 cm default cannot reach: Aron centre -6200 to paroches -5600 is 600 cm. The book gives NO number (see sources); the Gemara has the poles miraculously lengthen ('ויאריכו הבדים') to the paroches, so the length is fixed by the geometry.
poles.westStubNote: About the model's own pole overhang (18.86 mm x 1.471 = 27.7 cm) rounded up; the west stub stays inside the Kodesh (west wall at X -6700). Override: -AronPolesWestStubCm=<cm>.

paroches.source: SourceAssets/sanctuary-detail/DoorsParochesV1/native-import-20260907T184828Z.json reopenedReadback; cloth hangs 6.6 cm in front of the Heichal face of the Kodesh wall (X -5600).
paroches.intentionalIntersectionNote: The pole tips end 3.4 cm inside the cloth drape AABB (-5593.4..-5576.5): the 'bulge'. Cloth and hem are excluded from the clearance check and the penetration is recorded.

poles.kodeshEnvelopeNote: Kodesh room plus the amah-traksin zone (-5700..-5600) and the paroches cloth drape up to its Heichal face (-5576.5): the pole tips may sit inside the cloth but never beyond it. The doorway is 350 cm wide (Y +-175) and 300 cm high (Z 925..1225): both poles (Y +-67, Z 975..983) pass through it; the open Kodesh door leaves sit at Y +-158..174.

clearance.rule: Same rules as release_import_thirdparty_vessels.py: each planned pole AABB must not overlap any mesh-bearing actor except the paroches cloth/hem (intentional), terrain tiles, and hollow architecture unions whose verified constituent boxes are not hit. A blocker refuses the run BEFORE anything is saved.

verification.compareRule: Numeric location/rotation/scale fields and AABB corners only; str(Transform) is never compared. Capsule facets (32 steps) keep the radius within 0.02 cm of nominal.

sources.orientation: Task brief: Aron length north-south (Rambam Beit HaBechirah, as cited in the brief); poles east-west protruding into the paroches (Yoma 54a).
sources.yoma54a: Yoma 54a: the poles pressed against and protruded into the paroches and appeared like two breasts ('דוחקין ובולטין בפרוכת ונראין כשני דדי אשה').
sources.menachot98: Menachot 98a-b: 'ויאריכו הבדים' - the poles reached the paroches without tearing through; the poles were laid across the WIDTH of the Aron (two carriers between the poles).
sources.rashiShemot25_12: Rashi Shemot 25:12: the rings sat at the upper corners near the kaporet, two on each side across the width, the Aron's length (2.5 amot) separating pole from pole.

book.title: Lishchno Tidreshu (the user's book), reference-page scans in 'mikdash book/reference-pages'

pages.content: Yechezkel 41:3 - Kodesh entrance; 'דלתות פתוחות': the Kodesh HaKodashim doors stayed open and 'והבדים [מוטות לנשיאה של הארון] בלטו בפרוכת'.

Picture ג7 'בדי הארון נוגעים בפרוכת ק"ק'; text: 'ונעשה נס שבדי ארון הברית [שני קרשים מצופים זהב, שהיו משני צדי הארון] האריכו ודחקו הפרוכת, ונראו כמו שני דדי אשה' (Yoma 54a, Tosafot Menachot 98b); Second Temple: amah traksin with two curtains.

Yechezkel 41:23 - 'ויאריכו הבדים ... ויראו ראשי הבדים מן הקדש על פני הדביר ולא יראו החוצה'; Menachot 98a: poles touch the paroches, do not tear out; 'הבדין דוחקין ובולטין בפרוכת ודומין כמין שני דדי אשה'. Picture כג4 'דלתות קדש הקדשים מזהב והבדים נוגעים בפרוכת'.
Abarbanel: the bulge showed the Kohen Gadol where the Aron stood; picture כג5 'בליטת הבדים בפרוכת קדש הקדשים'. No numeric pole length anywhere on these pages.

book.poleLengthNote: The book gives no length; its pictures draw the poles spanning from the Aron to the paroches, which is what the geometry rule reproduces.

limitations: Third-party art (CC BY-SA): the pole-less duplicate is a further derivative of davidgra11's 'Ark of the Covenant Box' and stays CC BY-SA with the attribution in SourceAssets/third-party/ATTRIBUTION-additions.txt; the new capsule poles are project geometry.

The four model rings stay on the east/west faces with a north-south axis (empty; the pole/ring fusion leaves a small open loop inside each ring bore). The new poles run beside the north/south faces and are not threaded through rings (no rings are modelled on the short faces). Optional -AronPolesDeleteRings removes the rings at the cost of ring-footprint holes in the wall.
Pole length (~680 cm) follows the Gemara's miracle geometry, not a measured number; radius 4 cm, gold material, hemispherical ends are modelling choices.
Pole height uses the model's own ring height (54 cm above the floor), not the brief's 'lower third' guess.
Geometric verification only: no visual, lighting, LOD, Nanite, performance or packaged acceptance.
